#1 · This check does not consider data:.
The validateLink function blocks protocols listed in BAD_PROTOCOLS but the CodeQL rule indicates 'data:' is not
considered. Since 'data:' URLs can execute JavaScript in certain contexts (e.g., iframe src, object data), this is
an incomplete blocklist. The function is reachable from multiple markdown parsing entry points (link, image,
autolink, reference, linkify) that process user-supplied markdown.
User-supplied URLs in markdown links, images, and autolinks → validateLink() returning true for 'data:' scheme
Checks on the path: trim(), toLowerCase(), colon check, BAD_PROTOCOLS blocklist
Attacker needs / exploit idea: Attacker provides a markdown link/image with a 'data:' URL (e.g.,
'![x](data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>)') and the application renders the output without additional
// url should be normalized at this point, and existing entities are decoded
The assign function copies all own enumerable properties from source objects to a target object without filtering
dangerous keys like __proto__, constructor, or prototype. Since Object.keys() returns these keys when they are own
properties (e.g., from JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"polluted":true}}')), an attacker controlling the options parameter
can pollute Object.prototype. This affects all objects in the application and can lead to denial of service, logic
bypasses, or remote code execution depending on how polluted properties are used downstream.
User-controlled options object passed to MarkdownIt constructor or set() method → MarkdownIt.prototype.set
calls utils.assign(this.options, options) at lib/index.js:341 → utils.assign iterates Object.keys(source) and
assigns each key to target at lib/common/utils.js:29 → If source contains __proto__, constructor, or prototype as
own properties, they are copied to target's prototype
Attacker needs / exploit idea: Pass a malicious options object with __proto__ property to markdown-it: `const md =
require('markdown-it')({ __proto__: { isAdmin: true } })` or `md.set({ __proto__: { env: { NODE_OPTIONS: '--require
/tmp/evil' } } })`. The polluted prototype properties may be inherited by other objects and affect a
